blocks.text: AI Security discovers and monitors AI resources across your cloud environments, including models, agents, data stores, workloads, and guardrails. The ServiceNow integration lets you push these discovered assets and their associated security issues into ServiceNow, so your IT, security, and risk teams can manage AI resources within the same governance and compliance workflows they already use.
Ensure that your ServiceNow instance is online.
Ensure you do the following before you integrate AI Security with ServiceNow:

blocks.item: 1. Create a ServiceNow User.
To create a ServiceNow user, do the following:
Log in to your ServiceNow instance.
Navigate to User Administration > Users.
Click New.
Enter all the relevant fields to create a new user and click Submit.
To assign roles to the created user, go to User Administration > Users.
Select the user that you would like to assign the role to.
Add the following roles to the user:
import_admin
import_set_loader
import_transformer
See image.
Click Save.
2. Create an Inbound Integration.
To create an inbound integration, do the following:
Navigate to Inbound Integrations in your ServiceNow instance.
Click New Integration.
See image.
Select OAuth – Client Credential Grant as the authentication type.
See image.
In the New record page, enter the following details for the connection:
Name: Enter a name for the record.
Provider name: Select the provider name from the drop-down menu.
OAuth application user: Enter the user name you created in Create a ServiceNow User step.
Client ID: Copy the generated Client ID to a secure location. These credentials are required to complete the integration.
Client Secret: Copy the generated Client secret to a secure location. These credentials are required to complete the integration.
In the Configure auth scopes section, enter:
Auth scope: Select the auth scope from the drop-down menu.
Limit Authorization to the following APIs:
Table API
Import Set API
Enable Allow access only to APIs in selected scope.
Click Save.

blocks.text: To integrate AI Security with ServiceNow:

blocks.item: Go to Administration > External Integrations.
Under ITSM Integrations, click Add.
See image.
In the Integration Details section, do the following:
Integration Name: Enter a unique name for the integration.
IT Service: Select ServiceNow.
See image.
Click Next.
In the ITSM Details section, do the following:
ServiceNow Hostname: Enter the ServiceNow hostname.
Authentication Method: OAuth 2.0 is selected by default.
Client ID: Enter the Client ID created in the prerequisites section.
Client Secret: Enter the Client ID created in the prerequisites section.
Click Test Connection to validate the ServiceNow connection. A confirmation message appears if the connection is successful. If not, then check the previous steps and try again.
Click Next.
See image.
In the AI Infrastructure & Issues section, do the following:
Select one of the following:
AI Assets types: To sync asset types such as Agents, Data stores, MCP servers, Guardrails, Models, Workloads, Software Libraries, Code Repositories and Identities with ServiceNow.
Select All: To sync all available asset types.
Issues: Enable the Issues toggle to push findings to ServiceNow.
Select the method to determine how the discovered issues must be routed:
Create Ticket: Push issues to the ServiceNow Import Set (staging) table.
Import Set Table: Push issues directly to the ServiceNow Incident table.
Click Next.
In the Import Set Tables section, do the following:
Table Prefix: Enter a table prefix for the import set tables to be created in ServiceNow and click Check Tables.
Generated Table Names: Displays a preview of the Import Set table names that are created in your ServiceNow instance, based on the prefix you entered.
Provision Tables: Download the creation script to run it in ServiceNow.
Click Download Script to download the JavaScript setup script.
Open the downloaded script file and copy all the content.
Log in to your ServiceNow instance and open the JavaScript console.
Paste the copied script into the console and click Run Script.
The script automatically creates the required import set tables and the necessary roles.
See image.
Click Validate to validate the setup.
See image.
Return to the AI Security Admin Portal platform and click Check Tables.

Ensure that the user account configured for the inbound integration has the required ServiceNow roles to access the tables. Table validation may fail even if the tables exist, if the user lacks sufficient permissions.
Verify that the tables are successfully created, a green indicator confirms the setup is complete.
Click Save to finalize the integration.
After saving, the integration appears on the Integrations page. Allow up to an hour for the data to be pushed into the ServiceNow tables.
